agro_climatic_context: Intensively irrigated canal and tubewell system; high vulnerability to underground water depletion and terminal heat stress in wheat during March.
key_directives: Punjab Preservation of Subsoil Water Act: No farmer shall transplant paddy nursery before notified date (June 15-20) to curb summer water table decline.
Wheat: Timely sowing between November 1 to 20 is essential to ensure high tillering before temperatures rise in February.
Cotton: Sowing in south-western districts (Bathinda, Mansa, Sirsa) must finish by mid-May to prevent CLCuV (Cotton Leaf Curl Virus) and pink bollworm.
source: PAU Ludhiana & CCS HAU Hisar Extension Directives

agro_climatic_context: Semi-arid tropics with Vertisols (deep black soils) having high moisture-retention capacity; subject to prolonged dry spells during monsoon breaks.
key_directives: Cotton in Vidarbha and Marathwada: Sow after receiving at least 75-100 mm cumulative monsoon rain. Broad Bed and Furrow (BBF) improves in-situ rainwater conservation.
Tomato in Nashik and Pune belts: Staked cultivation with drip irrigation and silver-black plastic mulch significantly curbs fruit borer and fungal blights.
Onion: Nashik Kharif onion requires raised nursery beds to avoid damping off and purple blotch.
source: MPKV Rahuri & PDKV Akola Agronomic Recommendations

agro_climatic_context: Red sandy loams (Chalka) and medium black soils; hot summers, high incidence of sucking pests (thrips, whiteflies, mites).
key_directives: Cotton: High Density Planting System (HDPS) with compact non-Bt or Bt varieties at 80 cm x 20 cm spacing is recommended for Chalka soils.
Tomato in Madanapalle / Chittoor: Severe pressure of Tomato Pinworm (Tuta absoluta) and Leaf curl. Use pheromone traps and prophylactic neem sprays.
source: PJTSAU Hyderabad & ANGRAU Guntur Advisory Service

region: Eastern Lower Gangetic Plains (West Bengal & Odisha)
agro_climatic_context: Humid subtropical, alluvial river basins, heavy rainfall, high water table, and prone to pre-monsoon squalls (Kalbaishakhi).
key_directives: Jute: Sowing from mid-March to April enables harvest by July at 120 days, allowing timely transplanting of subsequent Aman paddy.

Retting of Jute: Use microbial retting consortium (CRIJAF Sona) @ 4 kg per quintal green jute plants in retting ponds to shorten retting time from 21 days to 12 days and upgrade fiber quality by 2 grades.
